blocks.text: git status compares the three areas and reports what differs. The short format is denser and easier to scan once you know the two-column code: the left column is the index (compared with HEAD), the right column is the working tree (compared with the index).

$ git status -sb
## main...origin/main [ahead 2, behind 1]
M  src/api.py        # staged modification
 M README.md         # unstaged modification
MM src/models.py     # staged, then modified again
A  src/stock.py      # new file, staged
D  legacy.py         # deletion, staged
R  util.py -> lib.py # rename, staged
?? scratch.txt       # untracked
UU config.yml        # unresolved merge conflict

The branch line ## main...origin/main [ahead 2, behind 1] tells you your local branch has 2 commits not yet pushed and the remote-tracking branch has 1 commit you have not integrated. This is based on your last fetch, not on live server state.
git diff: Comparing Any Two States

rows: Index vs HEAD (what will be committed)
Working tree vs HEAD (all uncommitted changes)
Tip of main vs tip of feature
Merge base of main and feature vs tip of feature (what the feature branch changed)
Only files under src/, compared with 3 commits ago

items: --stat: summary of files and line counts changed.
--name-only / --name-status: just the file list, useful in scripts and CI to detect which parts of a monorepo changed.
--word-diff: highlights changed words instead of whole lines, ideal for prose and config.

* 9c1e2f7 (HEAD -> feature/stock) Add stock endpoint
| * 4b8d0a1 (origin/main, main) Fix CORS config
|/
* 71a3e55 Add inventory model

rows: Include the patch for each commit
Only commits that touched that path
Follow a single file across renames
Follow only the main line, hiding merged branch internals

blocks.text: git show <commit> displays one commit's metadata and diff. git show HEAD:src/api.py prints a file as it existed in a specific commit, without checking anything out.
This is a classic interview question, and the confusing part is that the notation means different things in log and diff.

rows: Commits reachable from B but not from A (what B has that A lacks)
Same as git diff A B: tip-to-tip comparison
Commits reachable from either but not both (symmetric difference)
Changes on B since the merge base of A and B

blocks.src: generate: commit graph where main and feature diverge from a common ancestor commit M; main has commits m1, m2; feature has f1, f2; highlight f1, f2 for 'git log main..feature', highlight m1, m2, f1, f2 for 'git log main...feature', and show an arrow from M to f2 for 'git diff main...feature'
blocks.alt: Two-dot and three-dot notation on a diverged history
blocks.caption: git log main..feature lists f1 and f2. git diff main...feature shows what feature changed since it branched off.

blocks.text: GitHub's Pull Request "Files changed" view is a three-dot diff: it shows what your branch changed since the merge base, not how your branch differs from the current tip of main. That is why new commits on main do not appear in your PR's diff.
